<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par115 />was so fully established, that it could be used not only in such strange cases, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יָכְֽלוּ דַבְּרוֹ לְשָׁלֹם|translate=they could not speak to him peaceably}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=לְשִׂטְנוֹ|translate=to be an adversary to him}}, but ultimately even in the 1st sing., as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=לְתִתִּי|translate=to give me leave}} [{{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אָבָה יַבְּמִי}} ''he will not perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto me''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=4|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי|translate=that it may not grieve me!}}]

{{GHGmargin-letter|115|d}}
3. The power of governing like a verb is also retained in those verbal nouns which, although originally secondary forms of the infinitive, have fully acquired the value of nouns, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=11|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעָה אֶת־יְהֹוָה}} (prop. to know the Lord) ''the knowledge of the Lord''; {{GHGheb|text=לְיִרְאָה אֹתִי|translate=to fear me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=12|hidebook=1}}; an accusative follows {{GHGheb|text=לְאַֽהֲבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=12}}, 15, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=6}} (cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=3|verse=1}}); {{GHGheb|text=לַֽהֲנָפָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּשִׂנְאַת יְהֹוָה אֹתָ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=27}}; after verbal nouns formed with the prefix {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} (cf. {{GHGpar|45|e}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=9}}. The accusative of the object likewise remains after infinitives (or their secondary forms) which have the article, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=16}}, or a suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=4}}, &c., 28:4, 6, 29:19 f., 30:15, 38:5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|115|e}}
'''2.''' The subject of the action represented by the infinitive is mostly placed immediately<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=30}} the subject of {{GHGheb|text=כִּרְאֹת}} is wanting (but {{GHGheb|text=כְּשָׁמְעוֹ}} follows); the original reading was undoubtedly {{GHGheb|text=כִּרְאֹתוֹ}}, and the text is now in a state of confusion; verse 30''a'' should come before verse 29''b''. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=4}} the subject, although not indicated, is easily supplied from the context. The infinitive in such cases is best rendered in English by a passive.</ref> after it, either in the ''genitive'' or ''nominative''. The subject is in the genitive ({{GHGpar|33|c}}) whenever it has the form of a noun-suffix, and also when the infinitive has the termination of the constr. st. fem. sing. (see ''f''); probably also in many other cases, where the infinitive in form and meaning is used more like a substantive, and accordingly governs like a noun. On the other hand, the subject of the infinitive is certainly to be regarded as a nominative, when it is separated from the infinitive by any insertion, and according to certain indications (see ''g'') very probably in many other instances.

{{GHGmargin-letter|115|f}}
Rem. 1. Examples of genitives of the subject after infinitives in the connective form are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּשִׂנְאַת יְהֹוָה אֹתָ֫נוּ}} prop. ''in the Lord’s hating us''; cf. 7:8, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=11}}. The subject of the infinitive is probably also to be regarded as genitive in such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=1}} ''and there was no water'' {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁתֹּת הָעָם|translate=for the people to drink}} (prop. for the drinking of the people), and in cases like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=בְּלֶ֫דֶת הָגָר}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=3}}, 4, 33:38, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=133|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=7|verse=3}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|115|g}}
2. Examples in which the subject is separated from the infinitive by an insertion, and hence must certainly be regarded as a nominative, are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהִסָּ֫תֶר שָׁם פֹּֽעֲלֵי אָ֫וֶן|translate=that the workers of iniquity may hide themselves there}} (prop. for the hiding themselves there the workers of iniquity); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=10}}, and below, ''i''. The subject is likewise to be regarded as a ''nominative'', whenever the ''Lamedh'' is prefixed to the infinitive by means of a pretonic Qameṣ (cf. ''b'' above), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=לָשׂוּם הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ אֶל־לִבּוֹ}},<section end=par115 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
